chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: After-hours party near Boston; Joe Benjamin's drowsy drinking and earlier car wreck
summary: A club owner hosts the group, and Malachi recalls Joe Benjamin falling asleep after drinking and crashing his Cadillac near a truck.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: One night a fellow asked us to come out to his place. He had a place out on Route 9, I think, a club, where they closed something like 1 o'clock out there, and I think we played until about 3. But he invited us out, Sarah and the people in the group, to come out and just have free drinks and food and whatever, because he liked Sarah and he liked music. So we decided to go. We went out there. I think Sarah rode out there with Joe Benjamin, and I was with another friend of mine, a girl from New York, and I think somebody else was with us. And we had about four cars that went out there. And I think George, Sarah's husband, was driving her car.

Anyway, we get out there and we're drinking and whooping it up until about I guess 6 o'clock in the morning. Joe Benjamin was a guy, whenever he drank... I don't know whether it was some sort of disease you'd call it or something he had, that he could start up and have a conversation with you, and the next thing you know, he would be snoring, asleep. Just

why this happened or how it would happen, I don't know. I guess there must be some kind of name for a situation like that. Because I had had an accident with him prior to this engagement, where we were riding down... I think we were coming from Syracuse, New York, and we were going down to Atlantic City. In riding with him, sometimes he drove a little bit carelessly. But at times I would mention things to him that I think he should do while he was driving, and he would immediately put me in my place by talking to me to the effect of not to be a back-seat driver, and he wouldn't try to hurt himself.

So finally, one morning he and I were riding from Syracuse to Atlantic City, and I saw him coming up very close on this truck -- we were behind it. So I'm not going to say anything, until it got so very close, I said something to the effect, "Damn, Joe, look out!" And when he came to himself, he'd (?) the car and tore all of the right fender off of it, and just messed it up. It was his car; he had a Cadillac. Well, that just turned out to be an "I told you" situation. I never did say that to him, because when incidents like that happen, it's not the proper time.
